title: Taj Mahal - Steve Gerrard 2001
credits: Taj Mahal; landowner Feliciano Tun Canul; total explored/surveyed guidelines 23,150 ft (7,640 m); first explorers (March-May 1995) Nancy DeRosa, Tony DeRosa, Steve Gerrard, Wayne Nefzger; known continued explorers Bernie Birnbach, Kate Lewis, Dan Lins, Christophe A. Le Maillot, German Yanez Mendoza, Bil Phillips, Daniel Riordan, Christian Thomas; 2000 survey team Jeronimo Aviles, Vince Dekan, Vinnie Dekan, Steve Gerrard, Herve Gordon, Doug Hoyt, Marika Jasper, Kate Lewis, Lamont Machemer, Judy Pierson, Merle Pierson, Donald Reiland, Benji Sacriston, Steve Serras, Gonzalo Vaccaluzzo; Compass cave map by Steve Gerrard, March 2001
placementWhy: Moderate (about 10-20 m around Taj Mahal, worse at the far ends): free similarity fit on three points, residuals 11, 7 and 4 m; 0.578 m/px, rotated 3 degrees clockwise (the map has no north arrow or scale bar left on this scan). Points: Cenote Taj Mahal's main pool on the database's Taj Mahal (Open Caves source, taken on site; the user's dive log gives the same point) - the map's pool drawing then covers the sandy clearing of the cenote, Points of Light on its west part; Cenote Mangrova on the centre of the ring-shaped pond (open water round a mangrove island) 200 m west, the only open water on the imagery; City of Agre's south-west pool (where the line arrives) on a dark open-water pool 375 m east. Cross-checked: the two Expedition Yuc maps (Cenote Taj Mahal 1996, Taj Mahal - Minotauro 1997/98, with scale bars and north) give the same Taj Mahal - Mangrova - City of Agre (their 'Estrela' collapse) geometry within 20-40 m and no rotation; City of Agre's outline sits just west of the placed Reato 2013 Minotauro walls, which reach a pool 30 m south of the fit pool (their Cenote Estrella), as the Yuc 97/98 map draws Estrela's collapse joined to Minotauro's passages; no overlap. Buena Vista is the weak end: the map puts it 553 m north of Taj Mahal, the Yuc maps 464-497 m; a pale rocky gap in the canopy at their position lies 50 m south of this map's pool (check point, not used). Sacrado lands 57 m from where the Yuc 96 map puts Sagrada (C5).

trace.why: b/w Compass line plot (guidelines only, no walls), traced as lines (inkLevel 200, bridgePx 5: the scan's thin lines are pale and broken at the default level). Every label is excluded and every label arrow erased by hand (automatic leader removal off: it took survey lines). Cenote pools (hatched or black outlines) are not survey and are erased where the lines only reach them (Buena Vista's black pool, Mangrova, Points of Light, Taj Mahal, Sacrado, Twin Cenotes, Nachich, City of Agre's two pools); where a line runs through the drawing (Buena Vista's three hatched slopes, Sugarbowl, Room of Reflections, the airdomes, Room of Cheers) the drawing is left as traced, so the line stays whole. City of Agre's outline (a large collapse, mostly dry and tree-covered - orange on the Yuc 97/98 map) is kept. poolInsides isn't used: it dropped whole lines next to the slopes. Gaps left as on the map (jumps): the short west stub south of Buena Vista and the branch below it stop about 10 px short of the main line.

symbols.why: Compass line plot by Steve Gerrard (2001), b/w: no legend, no overlined depths, no letter codes, no water-flow arrows (the arrowheads on the lines are line arrows, not flow). Everything added by hand: named places at what their label or arrow points to; 'Deep Bone Room' kept as bones (at the small circle its arrow points to); the "68'" beside it is taken as a depth in feet (the apostrophe; the map gives no other depth) - an assumption. 'MAJOR RESTRICTIONS' (two arrows) as major restrictions, 'Restriction' and 'RESTRICTIONS' (one arrow) as restrictions. 'The Constrictor' kept as a place name (a named restriction, how tight not said).
